name: Ferrari 212 Export Vignale Spyder
description:
The 212 Export was the short-wheelbase competition version of Ferrari's 212, built from 1951 on the same lines as the 166 and 195 before it: Gioacchino Colombo's V12 bored out again, now to 2,562 cc, in an elliptical-section steel tube frame that the later cars replaced with the stiffer Tuboscocca. Around twenty-seven were built, bodied to order by Vignale, Touring and Ghia.

It won the 1951 Tour de France with Pagnibon and Barraquet, and the Coppa Inter-Europa at Monza with Vittorio Marzotto. By 1955 it was four years old and still being entered by privateers against sports-racers half a decade newer.

Technical specifications

Engine: front longitudinal 60° V12, light alloy block and heads, two valves per cylinder, single overhead camshaft per bank
Bore and stroke: 68 x 58.8 mm
Unitary and total displacement: 213.54 / 2,562.51 cc
Compression ratio: 8:1
Maximum power: 150 bhp at 6,500 rpm
Transmission: dry single-plate clutch, five speeds plus reverse, conventional differential
Chassis: elliptical-section steel tubes
Front suspension: independent, double wishbones, transverse lower leaf spring
Rear suspension: live axle, twin semi-elliptic leaf springs each side
Wheelbase, front and rear track: 2,250 / 1,270 / 1,250 mm
Kerb weight: 800 kg
Maximum speed: 193 km/h; 0–100 km/h in 9 s, 0–160 km/h in 22 s
